associations.note: Paired mex systems can admit an exact low-memory complementary law. For T, that means the only serious low-memory hope is an explicit border theorem with sparse corrections, not a loose feature heuristic.

The previous-column term is genuinely T-specific because it is created by the paired mex rule itself. That makes it better than generic divisor-density summaries, but it is only one marked point inside a whole covered interval.

associations.idea: Offset is a mesoscopic state, not yet a certificate
associations.note: The left offset tracks record growth inside the record set, but the current corpus already shows that high offset alone does not isolate records from ordinary late windows.

If a frontier law exists, it likely looks like abelian-network stabilization or least action: the border reached after legal local updates should be canonical. Anything weaker is probably just descriptive bookkeeping.

Any candidate based only on local product coverage, interval filling, or divisor-in-an-interval language must be benchmarked directly against surrogate product windows that erase the paired-mex provenance.
Late composite-only records force the mechanism away from prime-support rhetoric and toward semigroup geometry, border order, or stabilization.

associations.idea: Record-only trend fitting is a trap
associations.note: A bounded-memory story can look impressive when regressed only on record windows. The real test is whether it still beats matched nonrecords and Ford-style surrogates on held-out data.

The right abstraction may be a coarse complementary backbone for (r_n, c_n) plus a sparse correction process whose spikes create records. If those spikes do not stay structured, bounded memory is likely dead.
If anchor and offset fail, the remaining bounded-memory candidate is structural rather than pointwise: a bounded family of frontier witness graphs, Betti defects, or forest-like interval profiles.

Adjacent greedy systems split into two classes: exact complementary laws on one side and irregular large-gap behavior on the other. T is probably forced into one of those two archetypes rather than a soft middle ground.

Viewing uncovered values near the frontier as vacancies suggests a deterministic jamming question: are record windows rare fluctuations around a bounded jam length, or evidence that the jam length itself drifts?
A real T-specific law should survive equivalent schedules and axis swap, but it should not survive arbitrary surrogate rewiring. That robustness profile matters more than raw predictive score.

forced_bridges.from: Wythoff and complementary Beatty sequence theory
forced_bridges.mechanism: Treat (r_n, c_n) as an almost-complementary pair generated by paired mex, fit a coarse complementary skeleton, and move all record behavior into a residual correction process. If the residual alphabet is not sparse or stable, the backbone explanation fails.

Reinterpret row choice, column choice, and coverage insertion as commuting defect-repair updates on the frontier. The target invariant is a canonical stabilized border pair and a least-action style avalanche statistic.

forced_bridges.to: Failure mode of bounded-memory T explanations
forced_bridges.mechanism: Use the modular-vs-irregular dichotomy from greedy additive sequences as a template: either T windows collapse into finitely many frontier archetypes, or local-looking regularity is illusory and large gaps escape bounded memory.

Replace chosen witnesses by factorization-complexity summaries such as branching, catenary-style distance, or Betti counts. A bounded-memory mechanism could survive here even if raw witness certificates already failed.

forced_bridges.from: Random sequential adsorption and parking processes
forced_bridges.to: Late record windows as vacancy clusters
forced_bridges.mechanism: Model uncovered frontier values as a deterministic vacancy field whose leftmost vacancy is always repaired by mex. Boundedness becomes a cluster-tail question instead of an individual-witness question.

anomaly_results.result: In the stored 10^6-step baseline, 6 of the 17 row-gap records are prime-free, and the current largest record gap 30 is entirely composite.
anomaly_results.implication: Any surviving bounded-memory law must work without skipped-prime support; prime-placement stories are auxiliary at best.

anomaly_results.result: Nonrecord windows reach left offset 24 with gaps 25 and 26, while the largest true record has left offset 16. Among the 451 windows with left offset at least 15, only 2 are records.
anomaly_results.implication: Offset-before is enriched at records but is far from sufficient. A raw anchor/offset backbone already fails as a standalone separator.

anomaly_results.result: Within the 17 true records, gap size and left offset have strong correlation (about 0.88), but nonrecords populate the same high-offset regime.
anomaly_results.implication: In-record regressions will overstate progress. The real bottleneck is discriminating records from matched controls, not summarizing the record set itself.

anomaly_results.result: Late records do not share one split pattern: gap 25 has left/right split 21/4, gap 28 has 11/17, and gap 30 has 16/14.
anomaly_results.implication: A single one-parameter anchor law is unlikely. If bounded memory survives, it needs residual classes, schedule observables, or a higher-order structural invariant.

anomaly_results.constraint: Existing schedule robustness is already partially spent
anomaly_results.result: The repo already treats row_immediate as identical to the baseline and column_immediate as the axis swap.
anomaly_results.implication: A schedule-invariant frontier law must deliver more than superficial update-order robustness; it needs a true canonical stabilization observable.

anomaly_results.constraint: Witness compression already failed at the pointwise level
anomaly_results.result: The stored analyses report that chosen-witness summaries do not collapse to a stable small alphabet, even though late full witness graphs remain sparse enough to keep a structural fallback alive.
anomaly_results.implication: If all bounded-memory explanations fail, it will be because even the structural frontier summaries match Ford-style surrogates; if any survive, they will be graph-level rather than witness-token level.

steering_directions.direction: Run a three-way matched-control test for anchor and offset features
steering_directions.rationale: The cheap corpus check already shows offset enrichment without separation. The next honest test is true records versus matched nonrecords versus Ford-style surrogate product windows.
steering_directions.first_step: Build a window table with true late records, size-and-scale matched nonrecords, and surrogate product windows matched on gap length, local factor budget, and prime content. Evaluate monotone models on left offset, right offset, offset change, and anchor rank.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If T-specific bounded memory is real, those features retain held-out lift against both control families. If the lift vanishes against surrogates, bounded memory has collapsed into Ford overlap.

steering_directions.direction: Promote only an exact complementary-residual backbone
steering_directions.rationale: Wythoff-style paired mex laws are the clean positive control. The local anomalies suggest that a coarse scalar offset is too weak; only a complementary backbone plus sparse residual process remains credible.
steering_directions.first_step: Fit a piecewise complementary model to (r_n, c_n), then log residual spikes, residual sign patterns, and residual run lengths around every late record and matched control window.
steering_directions.expected_signal: A live backbone shows sparse residual support, repeatable residual classes, or bounded residual memory near records. Diffuse or growing residual complexity kills the low-memory lane.

steering_directions.direction: Test a genuine schedule-invariant stabilization law
steering_directions.rationale: Abelian-network style invariance is the only bounded-memory form that could survive even if simple offsets fail, because it upgrades descriptive geometry into a theorem-shaped object.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement legal asynchronous and batched frontier-update schedules from identical snapshots, then compare the stabilized border pair, total firing count, maximal defect depth, and avalanche diameter.
steering_directions.expected_signal: The same stabilized border pair and closely aligned avalanche statistics across schedules would keep this lane alive. One honest counter-schedule with different stabilization kills it.

steering_directions.direction: Use prime-free records as the primary benchmark family
steering_directions.rationale: Prime-free records are the cleanest place to separate T-specific semigroup geometry from prime-support folklore.
steering_directions.first_step: Create a prime-free-only benchmark table containing every prime-free record and matched prime-free nonrecord windows, then rerun the anchor/residual tests without any prime-derived covariates.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Any real bounded-memory law should survive intact on the prime-free slice. A collapse there means the signal was secretly prime-mediated or surrogate-driven.

steering_directions.direction: Keep witness-forest and Betti-style invariants as the fallback bounded-memory lane
steering_directions.rationale: Pointwise witness compression has already failed, but structural witness graphs may still encode a bounded frontier type that is more specific than product density.
steering_directions.first_step: Export full witness graphs for every late record and matched controls, then compute cycle rank, arboricity, component profile, Betti-style branching counts, and catenary-like distances under two canonicalizations.
steering_directions.expected_signal: A live fallback shows bounded or slowly growing structural complexity in true T records that is not reproduced by matched nonrecords or surrogate windows.

steering_directions.direction: Treat perturb-and-swap robustness as a hard gate
steering_directions.rationale: A genuine T law should survive equivalent schedules and axis swap but should be brittle under small admissibility perturbations or surrogate rewiring. That pattern distinguishes mechanism from generic density.
steering_directions.first_step: Measure the best candidate invariant on baseline, row_immediate, column_immediate, and one mild admissibility perturbation, then compare with product-set surrogates.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Equivalent schedules preserve the invariant, the axis swap relabels it, and mild non-equivalent perturbations break it. If everything preserves it, the invariant is probably generic rather than T-specific.

validation_checks.check: Require held-out evaluation where anchor/offset features beat both a gap-length-only baseline and a local-product-density baseline on true records versus matched nonrecords and surrogates.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Consistent lift remains after conditioning on scale, gap length, and local divisor budget, with no collapse on surrogate windows.
validation_checks.fail_signal: The features explain records only inside the record set, or lose their lift once the Ford-style nulls are introduced.

validation_checks.check: Measure residual alphabet size, residual run-length entropy, and residual-memory depth as the horizon grows, and compare with matched controls.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Residuals stay sparse, repeatable, and horizon-stable, with record windows concentrated in a small number of residual classes.
validation_checks.fail_signal: Residual complexity grows with the horizon or looks no different from nonrecords and surrogates.

validation_checks.check: From identical frontier snapshots, run multiple legal asynchronous schedules and verify whether the stabilized border pair and defect statistics agree up to axis relabeling.
validation_checks.pass_signal: All schedules stabilize to the same border state and expose one or two schedule-independent observables correlated with record formation.
validation_checks.fail_signal: Different legal schedules stabilize differently, or the only invariant is trivial symmetry already known from the repo.

validation_checks.check: Repeat the candidate tests on prime-free records and prime-free matched controls with all prime-derived variables removed.
validation_checks.pass_signal: The same mechanism survives with nearly unchanged performance and interpretation on the prime-free slice.
validation_checks.fail_signal: Performance collapses once prime-bearing windows are removed, showing the claimed mechanism was not truly semigroup-based.

validation_checks.check: Compare frontier graph invariants against matched nonrecords and surrogate windows under at least two witness canonicalizations.
validation_checks.pass_signal: True T records retain a stable low-complexity structural profile that surrogates do not reproduce.
validation_checks.fail_signal: The structural summaries are canonicalization-sensitive or are matched by Ford-style surrogates, eliminating the last bounded-memory refuge.

validation_checks.check: Demand the characteristic robustness profile: preserved under equivalent schedules, relabeled under axis swap, but broken by non-equivalent admissibility perturbation or surrogate rewiring.
validation_checks.pass_signal: Exactly that selective robustness pattern appears.
validation_checks.fail_signal: Either the invariant breaks under equivalent schedules, or it survives every perturbation and therefore looks generic rather than T-specific.

sub_problem: Can a T-specific low-memory anchor/offset backbone or schedule-invariant frontier law separate true late record windows from matched controls and Ford-style surrogates, or do all such bounded-memory explanations fail?
